newsitem.title: MEXICO: Arrest warrants out for three Mexico businessmen.
newsitem.headline: Arrest warrants out for three Mexico businessmen.

text.p: Mexican authorities issued arrest warrants for three Mexican businessmen on Wednesday, the latest suspects in a high-profile crackdown on tax fraud, the Finance Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said it sought the arrest of Alfredo Hakim Aburto, head of a well-known construction firm that recently built an international terminal at the Mexico City airport.
It also went after his business partner and lawyer, Eli Mauricio Bello, and a Mexico City parking lot owner Juan Bernardo Sarquis Rodriguez.
The Finance Ministry said Hakim's firms had filed provisional value added tax payments of 11 million pesos ($1.45 million) that were never made.
Sarquis was accused of having deducted 8 million pesos ($1.1 million) in income tax from workers on his company's payroll and not paying it to the tax collector.

Wednesday's arrest warrants followed a massive police operation last Thursday to catch the editor of Mexico City daily El Universal, Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, also on charges of tax fraud. Ealy gave himself up to the authorities on Friday and was later released on bail.

El Universal protested the arrest as an attack on press freedom, but the Finance Ministry said it was a simple clamp-down on tax crimes amid what they said was a steep drop-off in tax receipts after last year's economic crisis.
